input: The thickness question at the compressor shell is, in the end, settled less by the pressure case on its own than by what corrosion will take from the wall over the life of the unit, and once the corrosion allowance is added, the compressor wall thickness stands at 51 mm. That figure frames the joint design that follows, including the flanged joint on the line toward the absorber, where the gasket choice has been argued on more grounds than the report allows. In this section the comparison is deliberately narrow: the two gasket materials are compared on temperature limit only, and the higher-rated material is preferred on that ground alone. Nothing in the comparison turns on $\Delta P$ across the joint, and nothing in it changes the NPSH position of the lean solvent pump, which sits outside the argument being made here. There is a practical edge to the narrowness of the comparison as well. The joint faces the temperature duty of the compressor discharge, and the gasket is the component that meets that duty directly; a lower-rated material would leave the joint as the weakest element in a wall that has just been thickened against corrosion, which is not a position the design can sensibly defend. The gasket choice at the joint is made on one ground. The two gasket materials are compared on temperature limit only, and the higher-rated material is preferred. The comparison carries no other property: seating load, relaxation, and chemical resistance are not weighed in this part of the report, and no preference stated here extends to them. The choice does not turn on $\Delta P$ across the joint, and it does not change the NPSH position of the lean solvent pump. The preference is limited to the temperature rating at the joint as lined up. A joint at a higher temperature duty would reopen the comparison on the same single ground, and a joint at a lower duty would still take the higher-rated material under the stated preference, because no second criterion has been admitted. The joint sits in a part of the unit where the temperature duty is set by the compressor discharge, and the gasket is the part of the joint that meets that duty directly. A material chosen on a lower rating would make the joint the weakest part of a wall that has been thickened for corrosion, and the report does not accept that position.
